tldr; Medical facility estimated I would owe them $700 for a procedure, beforehand, then actually bills me $12,000 afterwards. What can I do about it?

My medical insurance starts with $6000 deductible for in-network charges, $12,000 for out-of-network.

I had a minor surgical procedure done. Surgical center is new, trying to get onto insurance companies "in-network" lists, so is offering 80%+ discounts on various procedures. Doctor talks me into getting the surgery at this new facility because it's state-of-the-art and should still be cheaper.

Before getting the surgery, I get two separate estimates from two different people at the facility. Both times, they told me my total out-of-pocket expense (for everything) would be around $700. That seemed low, which is why I got the second estimate. They emphasized that it was an estimate, not an official quote, but seemed pretty sure of the number.

Now, three months later, my share of the bills is the full $12,000 out-of-network deductible. If I had gone with an in-network facility, my max out-of-pocket would have been $6,000 (insurance covers 100% beyond the deductible).

What, if any, recourse do I have at this point? How do I proceed?
Medical facility massively underestimated the cost of a procedure; do I have any recourse?

Same thing happened to me. I was told $500 max out of pocket for out of network. After my surgery, I got a bill for...not kidding at all...480k! Yes, that is four hundred and eighty thousand dollars. I kept getting calls from their collections. I told them to sue me, and try to explain how this surgery, if performed at a private hospital, would have cost a max 30k. Try explaining to a judge why you charged so much. Never heard from them again

First was there a complication? Did something happen in surgery to make it more expensive? That is very important for determining what to do next.

Second where do you live? My advice is to see a lawyer. Most states have a state bar referral system that offers you a free consult. From this point on get everything in writing, if the estimates are in writing save them. Now what you want to do is take this to the lawyer and then have your lawyer write them a letter stating the issue and the outcome desired. Your lawyer may contact your insurance company as well, due to the fact that your insurance company may be interested in the original estimate (they don't want to pay more if they don't have to).
